fact_text: EEA nationals (including Norwegians) working in France may apply for a carte de séjour citoyen UE/EEE/Suisse — Toutes activités professionnelles but it is not legally mandatory. fact_text: If a Norwegian employee is temporarily posted to France by a Norwegian employer, they may remain in the Norwegian social security system provided they hold an A1 certificate (formerly E101) issued by NAV Norway. Without the A1, French social security contributions apply from day one in France. The A1 is valid for a maximum initial posting period of 24 months under EC Regulation 883/2004 Art. 12.
entity_title: A1 Certificate — Workers Posted from Norway (EU/EEA nationals)

applies_to.curation_justification: EEA social-security coordination instrument as published → EEA
applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly assumed that anyone moving from Norway with a Norwegian employer needs an A1. The A1 belongs to posting, not to relocation: a permanent local move is covered by the state where the work is done. Action required: establish whether this is a posting before treating the A1 as a step, because the wrong branch changes who pays contributions and where.
applies_to.timing: before the first day of work in France
applies_to.scope_justification: The A1 certificate mechanism under Reg. 883/2004 Art. 12 applies by virtue of employment situation (posting by employer), not by the holder's nationality. Any worker posted from Norway to France — regardless of passport — remains on Norwegian social security and obtains an A1. The CLEISS page frames the rule in terms of employment in a Member State, with no nationality condition.
applies_to.conditional_on: Applies only where the move is a genuine temporary posting (détachement) and the Norwegian institution issues the A1. It does not apply to permanent France-based work, where French social security applies from the start under Reg. 883/2004 art. 11(3)(a).

fact_text: All persons starting work in France are assigned a French social security number (Numéro de Sécurité Sociale / NIR). For EEA employees, this is triggered automatically when the employer files the DPAE (Déclaration Préalable À l'Embauche) with URSSAF at least 8 days before the start of work. Self-employed persons receive their NIR upon completing business registration at the Guichet unique.
entity_title: French Social Security Number (NIR) — Assignment (EU/EEA nationals)

applies_to.curation_justification: fact_text describes the automatic DPAE-triggered mechanism for EEA employees → EEA (the universal first sentence is not separable from the EEA mechanism it documents)
applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you apply for a French social security number yourself. Actually for an employee it is triggered by the EMPLOYER filing the DPAE with URSSAF at least 8 days before your start date — if they file late or not at all, you have no NIR, and without a NIR there is no carte vitale and no reimbursement. Action required: confirm with HR that the DPAE has been filed before you start.
applies_to.timing: employer must file the DPAE at least 8 days before the start of work
applies_to.scope_justification: Affiliation to the French social security regime and assignment of an SS number is triggered by regular residence and work in France. fact_text: Under Article 4B of the French Code Général des Impôts (CGI), a person has their fiscal domicile in France — and is subject to unlimited French income tax on worldwide income — if any one of the following criteria is met: (1) their principal home (foyer) or principal place of sojourn is in France; (2) they exercise a professional activity in France whether salaried or not; or (3) the center of their economic interests is in France. A Norwegian arriving in France triggers French tax residency from the date any criterion is met.
entity_title: French Tax Domicile — CGI Article 4B (EU/EEA nationals)

applies_to.curation_justification: Art. 4B fiscal-domicile criteria apply to any person meeting them regardless of passport → universal, two records
applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed French tax residency starts after 183 days. Actually Article 4B of the CGI makes you tax-resident — on WORLDWIDE income — if ANY ONE of four tests is met, including having your main home or your centre of economic interests in France. You can be French tax-resident from arrival while still being paid from Norway. Action required: establish which side taxes you before the first payslip, not at year end.
applies_to.scope_justification: CGI Art. 4B as reproduced on the BOFiP page defines fiscal domicile in France by four criteria (foyer, séjour principal, activité professionnelle, centre des intérêts économiques) none of which reference nationality. The test is identical for EEA and non-EEA movers. Only one criterion needs to be met. Denis — a French national moving to Paris from Oslo — is subject to exactly the same test as any other person.
applies_to.conditional_on: person meets at least one of the four CGI Art. 4B criteria
applies_to.dedupe_note: An identical record was carried under a '_non_eea' key. CGI art. 4B does not vary by nationality, so the split was never meaningful and every mover read the paragraph twice.

evidence_quote: Sont ainsi considérées comme fiscalement domiciliées en France : les personnes qui ont sur le territoire français leur foyer ou le lieu de leur séjour principal, celles qui y exercent une activité professionnelle, salariée ou non, à moins qu'elles n'établissent que cette activité est exercée en France à titre accessoire, celles qui ont en France le centre de leurs intérêts économiques, les agents de l'État exerçant leurs fonctions ou chargés de mission dans un pays où ils ne sont pas soumis à un impôt personnel sur l'ensemble de leurs revenus.

fact_text: As both France and Norway are parties to EC Regulation No. 883/2004 on the coordination of social security systems (Norway via the EEA Agreement), a worker can only be subject to the social security legislation of one member state at a time. Upon genuine relocation from Norway to France and commencement of employment or self-employment in France, the worker falls under the French social security system exclusively and must register with CPAM and URSSAF.

applies_to.curation_justification: coordination rule between EEA states, applicable via the EEA Agreement → EEA
applies_to.non_obvious_note: Without this principle, a cross-border worker could be subject to social security legislation in multiple states simultaneously.
applies_to.scope_justification: The single-state principle under Reg. 883/2004 Art. 11 applies by employment situation, not nationality. The CLEISS page states it applies 'sans exception à toutes les situations.' A Norwegian national, a French national, or any other EU/EEA resident in the same employment situation is covered identically.
applies_to.conditional_on: person is simultaneously active or resident in more than one EEA state

evidence_quote: L'article 11 du règlement (CE) n° 883/2004 pose le principe de l'unicité de législation qui s'applique sans exception à toutes les situations.
